claims.text: As-synthesized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a large caloric response.
As-synthesized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
The proposed intervention is warm rolling or forging at 650–700°C followed by annealing at 800–900°C for 15–30 minutes.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will refine the alloy's microstructure and produce a heterogeneous grain-size distribution.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will induce a partial twin network.
A heterogeneous grain structure can improve load-bearing mechanical properties.
A partially twinned structure can contribute to high strength, ductility, and fracture toughness.
Refined grains and twin boundaries will deflect and blunt propagating cracks.
The processed alloy will have higher fracture toughness than the as-synthesized alloy.
The processed alloy will have greater load-bearing capacity and less cracking than the as-synthesized alloy.
The processed microstructure will preserve the lattice transformations required for the magnetocaloric response.
The processed microstructure will preserve the lattice transformations required for the barocaloric response.
The processed alloy will retain magnetocaloric performance similar to that of the as-synthesized alloy.
The processed alloy will retain barocaloric performance similar to that of the as-synthesized alloy.
The integrity and caloric benefits are expected to persist under refrigeration-relevant magnetic fields, pressure fields, temperatures, and service loadings.
The treatment is expected not to alter the alloy's inherent transformation temperatures.
Fine tuning of the processing window may be necessary to avoid undesirable shifts in caloric transition characteristics.
